cards.statement: Re-up rates from existing LPs were strong at 96 percent by capital, and the Fund welcomed new investors across three of the largest US public pension funds, two Asian sovereign wealth funds, and a number of European and North American family offices and endowments.

claims.claim: Re-up rates from existing LPs were strong at 96 percent by capital, and the Fund welcomed new investors across three of the largest US public pension funds, two Asian sovereign wealth funds, and a number of European and North American family offices and endowments.
claims.comment: The source states that re-up rates from existing LPs were 96% by capital and that new LPs include three of the largest US public pension funds, two sovereign wealth funds in Asia, and a number of family offices and endowments in Europe and North America. The description of re-up rates as strong is interpretive but consistent with the data.

cards.statement: The LP base spans 92 institutional investors across 26 countries.

claims.claim: The LP base spans 92 institutional investors across 26 countries.
claims.comment: The source notes that Fund V received commitments from 92 institutional investors across 26 countries, which matches the claim.

cards.statement: Fund V will be deployed across European industrial sectors with a particular focus on advanced manufacturing, energy transition, and specialty chemicals.

claims.claim: Fund V will be deployed across European industrial sectors with a particular focus on advanced manufacturing, energy transition, and specialty chemicals.
claims.comment: The source states that Fund V will be deployed across European industrial sectors with a particular focus on advanced manufacturing, energy transition, and specialty chemicals, matching the claim.

cards.statement: We anticipate 10 to 12 platform investments over the four-year deployment period, with typical equity tickets in the EUR 300 to 700 million range.

claims.claim: We anticipate 10 to 12 platform investments over the four-year deployment period, with typical equity tickets in the EUR 300 to 700 million range.
claims.comment: The source states that they anticipate making 10 to 12 platform investments over the four-year deployment period, with typical equity tickets in the EUR 300 to 700 million range. This directly supports the claim.

cards.statement: Our investment team has been preparing Fund V's pipeline for many months and we expect first capital calls in the second quarter of 2026.

claims.claim: Our investment team has been preparing Fund V's pipeline for many months and we expect first capital calls in the second quarter of 2026.
claims.comment: The source supports that investment teams have been engaging with prospective LPs and working throughout the year, which is a reasonable basis for saying they have been preparing the pipeline for many months. However, the expectation of first capital calls in the second quarter of 2026 is not mentioned anywhere in the source and is therefore not supported.

cards.statement: 3i Group delivered a total return of GBP 3.3 million for the six months to 30 June 2025, representing a 13% return on opening shareholders funds.

claims.claim: 3i Group delivered a total return of GBP 3.3 million for the six months to 30 June 2025, representing a 13% return on opening shareholders funds.
claims.comment: The source reports a total return of £3,291 million (≈£3.3 billion), not £3.3 million, and for the six months to 30 September 2025, not to 30 June 2025. The 13% return on opening shareholders’ funds is correct.

cards.statement: The private equity business generated gross investment returns of 14% for the period and accounted for the vast majority of the overall total return.

claims.claim: The private equity business generated gross investment returns of 14% for the period and accounted for the vast majority of the overall total return.
claims.comment: The source confirms that the Private Equity business delivered a gross investment return of 14%. However, it does not state that this accounted for the vast majority of the overall total return, so that portion is unsupported.

cards.statement: This was driven largely by Action, which continues to trade strongly.

claims.claim: This was driven largely by Action, which continues to trade strongly.
claims.comment: The source confirms that Action continued to trade strongly and that Action’s performance supported significant value growth, but it does not explicitly say that the Private Equity gross investment return was driven largely by Action. The attribution of primary causality is not supported.

cards.statement: The company’s new store expansion program is set for another record year with new stores in Switzerland and Romania being well received.

claims.claim: The company’s new store expansion program is set for another record year with new stores in Switzerland and Romania being well received.
claims.comment: The source states that Action’s new store expansion programme is on track for another record year and that new stores in Switzerland and Romania have been very well received, which supports this paraphrase.

cards.statement: Year to date like-for-like trading remains healthy despite weakening consumer confidence since the summer.

claims.claim: Year to date like-for-like trading remains healthy despite weakening consumer confidence since the summer.
claims.comment: The source notes that year-to-date like-for-like trading remains good despite weakening consumer confidence since the summer. Describing this as “healthy” is a reasonable paraphrase of “good.”

cards.statement: Net sales for the six months to 30 June 2026 amounted to EUR 11.2 billion, with like-for-like sales growth of 6.3%.

claims.claim: Net sales for the six months to 30 June 2026 amounted to EUR 11.2 billion, with like-for-like sales growth of 6.3%.
claims.comment: The source gives net sales of €11,229 million and LFL sales growth of 6.3% for the nine reporting periods ending on 28 September 2025, not for six months to 30 June 2026. Both the period and end date differ from the source.

cards.statement: Meanwhile, Action successfully completed several balance sheet transactions in October 2025.

claims.claim: Meanwhile, Action successfully completed several balance sheet transactions in October 2025.
claims.comment: The source confirms that Action completed two financing transactions in October 2025, which are balance sheet-related. However, it specifies two transactions, not “several,” so the implication of a larger number is not supported.

cards.statement: The company repriced EUR 3.1 billion of existing term debt, extending maturities and generating meaningful annual interest cost savings, while also raising an incremental EUR 1.6 billion of new term loan.

claims.claim: The company repriced EUR 3.1 billion of existing term debt, extending maturities and generating meaningful annual interest cost savings, while also raising an incremental EUR 1.6 billion of new term loan.
claims.comment: The source states that Action raised €1.6 billion of incremental term loan debt and repriced €3.1 billion of existing term loan debt, extending the maturity of a portion of the debt and generating annual interest cost savings of €14 million. Describing the savings as “meaningful” is acceptable paraphrase.

cards.statement: MAIT also completed a pro-rata redemption of shares, which generated significant proceeds for 3i.

claims.claim: MAIT also completed a pro-rata redemption of shares, which generated significant proceeds for 3i.
claims.comment: The pro-rata redemption of shares and related proceeds are attributed in the source to Action, not MAIT. MAIT is mentioned only in relation to its realisation, not a share redemption. This misattributes the transaction.

cards.statement: A portion of these proceeds was redeployed to acquire a further 2.2% stake in the business, which together with an earlier 2.2% stake purchase from AGIC, raised 3i’s stake in Action to 62.3%.

claims.claim: A portion of these proceeds was redeployed to acquire a further 2.2% stake in the business, which together with an earlier 2.2% stake purchase from AGIC, raised 3i’s stake in Action to 62.3%.
claims.comment: The source confirms that proceeds from Action’s capital restructuring were used to acquire a further 2.2% stake, following an earlier 2.2% acquisition from GIC, increasing 3i’s ownership to 62.3%. The draft incorrectly names the earlier seller as AGIC, not GIC.

cards.statement: Elsewhere, within the private equity portfolio, 3i completed the sale of MPM and signed an exit of MAIT during the period, which generated gross money multiples of 3.2x and 2.8x, respectively.

claims.claim: Elsewhere, within the private equity portfolio, 3i completed the sale of MPM and signed an exit of MAIT during the period, which generated gross money multiples of 3.2x and 2.8x, respectively.
claims.comment: The source confirms that 3i completed the realisation of MPM and signed the realisation of MAIT, generating sterling money multiples of 3.2x and 2.8x, respectively. Describing these as sales and exits is consistent with the source.

cards.statement: On the infrastructure side, gross investment returns stood at 9% for the period, outperforming expectations for the six-month period.

claims.claim: On the infrastructure side, gross investment returns stood at 9% for the period, outperforming expectations for the six-month period.
claims.comment: The source confirms a gross investment return of 9% for the Infrastructure business and notes that the infrastructure asset portfolio within 3iN outperformed its expected returns. However, it does not explicitly say that the 9% return itself was above expectations, so that part is not supported.

cards.statement: Performance was driven primarily by share price gains at 3i Infrastructure plc, which continues to report positive performance across its portfolio, including meaningful gains across essentially all of its investments.

claims.claim: Performance was driven primarily by share price gains at 3i Infrastructure plc, which continues to report positive performance across its portfolio, including meaningful gains across essentially all of its investments.
claims.comment: The source confirms that the 9% gross investment return was driven primarily by a 14% increase in 3i Infrastructure plc’s share price. It also notes that 3iN’s underlying portfolio continues to perform well, with a significant valuation uplift in TCR. However, the claim that there are meaningful gains across essentially all investments is not supported.

cards.statement: In light of the overall good performance of the portfolio, 3i declared a dividend of GBP 0.365 per share, which will be paid in January 2026.

claims.claim: In light of the overall good performance of the portfolio, 3i declared a dividend of GBP 0.365 per share, which will be paid in January 2026.
claims.comment: The source confirms a dividend per ordinary share of 36.5 pence for FY2026, to be paid in January 2026. Linking this to overall good performance is a reasonable inference from the strong results described.

cards.statement: Looking ahead, the UK government maintains its cautious stance on capital deployment into new investments, but remains open to selective allocations to lower-risk reinvestments in existing portfolio companies.

claims.claim: Looking ahead, the UK government maintains its cautious stance on capital deployment into new investments, but remains open to selective allocations to lower-risk reinvestments in existing portfolio companies.
claims.comment: The source attributes this cautious stance and selective allocation approach to 3i, not to the UK government. Assigning these views to the UK government directly contradicts the source.

cards.statement: HCIL Infrastructure’s performance for the six months to 31 December 2025 was positive and largely in line with expectations.

claims.claim: HCIL Infrastructure’s performance for the six months to 31 December 2025 was positive and largely in line with expectations.
claims.comment: The source refers to HICL Infrastructure (not HCIL) and covers the period from 1 October 2025 to 28 February 2026, not the six months to 31 December 2025. While it does say portfolio performance was in line with expectations, the company name and period are incorrect.

cards.statement: Across the portfolio, operational performance was robust, with average 30% EBITDA growth driven by capital expenditure, and resilient cashflow generation supporting HCIL’s dividend program.

claims.claim: Across the portfolio, operational performance was robust, with average 30% EBITDA growth driven by capital expenditure, and resilient cashflow generation supporting HCIL’s dividend program.
claims.comment: The source supports that operational performance across the portfolio was in line with expectations and resilient, and that capex programmes are driving EBITDA growth and cash generation supports the dividend and dividend cover. However, it does not mention an average 30% EBITDA growth figure, nor does it quantify EBITDA growth at that level, so that part is unsupported. The company name is also HICL, not HCIL.

cards.statement: Across the portfolio, growth investments continue to perform well, with significant investment in expansion programs driving EBITDA growth that continues to significantly outperform budgets.

claims.claim: Across the portfolio, growth investments continue to perform well, with significant investment in expansion programs driving EBITDA growth that continues to significantly outperform budgets.
claims.comment: The source confirms that HICL’s growth investments continue to perform well and that expansion capex programmes are delivering EBITDA in line with expectations. It does not state that EBITDA growth is significantly outperforming budgets; instead it says EBITDA is in line with expectations. The outperformance vs budgets is unsupported.

cards.statement: Among the significant holdings, Paris St. Germain High Speed performed well during the period, with international train path bookings slightly ahead of forecast.

claims.claim: Among the significant holdings, Paris St. Germain High Speed performed well during the period, with international train path bookings slightly ahead of forecast.
claims.comment: The source refers to London St. Pancras High Speed, not Paris St. Germain High Speed. It does say this asset performed well and that international train path bookings were slightly ahead of forecast, but the name/location of the asset in the claim conflicts with the source.

cards.statement: On the commercial front, progress has been made on adding a second international operator on the route, while Virgin Trains recently announced its intentions for cross-Channel operations from St. Germain.

claims.claim: On the commercial front, progress has been made on adding a second international operator on the route, while Virgin Trains recently announced its intentions for cross-Channel operations from St. Germain.
claims.comment: The source confirms progress toward a potential second international operator and that Virgin Trains announced intentions for cross-Channel operations and its approach to rolling stock procurement. However, the source locates this at St. Pancras, not St. Germain, so the place name is incorrect. The rest of the commercial-progress description is supported.

cards.statement: Elsewhere, TowerCo delivered 20 new towers during the past year and is actively progressing additional co-location opportunities, both of which are expected to support continued growth in EBITDA and valuation gains.

claims.claim: Elsewhere, TowerCo delivered 20 new towers during the past year and is actively progressing additional co-location opportunities, both of which are expected to support continued growth in EBITDA and valuation gains.
claims.comment: The source refers to Fortysouth, not TowerCo, and states that it delivered 16 new towers during the period, not 20 during the past year. It also notes incremental co-location opportunities and expected EBITDA growth, but does not mention valuation gains. The asset name, tower count, and time period conflict with the source, and the valuation gains element is unsupported.

cards.statement: The company also recently completed an oversubscribed refinancing, which will lead to an increase in debt servicing costs.

claims.claim: The company also recently completed an oversubscribed refinancing, which will lead to an increase in debt servicing costs.
claims.comment: The source confirms that Fortysouth completed an accretive refinancing that was about 30% oversubscribed. However, it states that this enabled a step-down in debt margins earlier than forecast, implying lower, not higher, debt servicing costs. The refinancing and oversubscription are supported; the claim that it will increase debt servicing costs conflicts with the source.

cards.statement: Meanwhile, Affinity Water appointed a new CFO with significant sector experience and stands to benefit from the French government’s recently published white paper on electricity sector reform.

claims.claim: Meanwhile, Affinity Water appointed a new CFO with significant sector experience and stands to benefit from the French government’s recently published white paper on electricity sector reform.
claims.comment: The source states that Affinity Water appointed a new CEO (Mark Garth) with sector experience from United Utilities, not a CFO. It also refers to a UK Government white paper on water sector reform, not a French government white paper on electricity sector reform. Both the role and the nature/jurisdiction of the white paper conflict with the source.

cards.statement: In October 2025, GP Industries announced that it intends to shift 75% of its global production capacity to its manufacturing sites in Southeast Asia to serve the US market amid tariffs, escalating oil prices and rising geopolitical tensions.

claims.claim: In October 2025, GP Industries announced that it intends to shift 75% of its global production capacity to its manufacturing sites in Southeast Asia to serve the US market amid tariffs, escalating oil prices and rising geopolitical tensions.
claims.comment: The source says the announcement was on 13 November 2025, not October; it does not mention a 75% figure or global production capacity; it refers to shifting production capacity to Southeast Asia to serve the US market amid tariffs and rising geopolitical tensions, but says nothing about escalating oil prices.

cards.statement: The company currently operates 15 facilities in Malaysia, two in Vietnam, and one in Thailand, alongside two other plants in the UK and one plant in China, which will now focus primarily on the European market.

claims.claim: The company currently operates 15 facilities in Malaysia, two in Vietnam, and one in Thailand, alongside two other plants in the UK and one plant in China, which will now focus primarily on the European market.
claims.comment: The source states three facilities in Malaysia, two in Vietnam, and one in Thailand, plus two plants in the UK. It does not mention 15 facilities in Malaysia or a single plant in China. It also says the China facility will focus on European and Asian markets, not only the European market.

cards.statement: The capacity adjustments are intended to streamline supply chains to meet country-of-origin requirements while improving the cost structure and enhancing site security.

claims.claim: The capacity adjustments are intended to streamline supply chains to meet country-of-origin requirements while improving the cost structure and enhancing site security.
claims.comment: The source supports that capacity changes are to streamline supply chains to meet country-of-origin requirements and maintain cost competitiveness (improve cost structure). It does not mention enhancing site security at all, so that part is unsupported.

cards.statement: Meanwhile, Silver Hill Technology (parent of GP Industries) is planning an investment program in Johor, Malaysia, to produce next-generation batteries to support data centres.

claims.claim: Meanwhile, Silver Hill Technology (parent of GP Industries) is planning an investment program in Johor, Malaysia, to produce next-generation batteries to support data centres.
claims.comment: The source identifies Gold Peak Technology Group as the Hong Kong-listed parent and as the entity planning a multi-million-dollar investment in Johor to produce next-generation batteries to support data centres. It does not mention Silver Hill Technology, so naming it as the parent and investor conflicts with the source.

cards.statement: GP Industries is the largest producer of consumer batteries globally, producing over 60 billion batteries annually, which are bartered through 1 million outlets worldwide.

claims.claim: GP Industries is the largest producer of consumer batteries globally, producing over 60 billion batteries annually, which are bartered through 1 million outlets worldwide.
claims.comment: The source describes GP Industries as the world’s second-largest producer of consumer batteries, not the largest, and says it produces over six billion batteries annually, sold (not bartered) through one million outlets worldwide. The draft inflates both the ranking and the production volume and changes the verb from sold to bartered.

cards.statement: ClearPoint Neuro announced in April 2026 its financial results for the first quarter of 2026.

claims.claim: ClearPoint Neuro announced in April 2026 its financial results for the first quarter of 2026.
claims.comment: The source states the press release announcing first quarter 2026 results is dated May 13, 2026, not April 2026. The quarter referenced is correct, but the month is not.

cards.statement: The company delivered 43% year-on-year growth in revenue to USD 12.1 million, driven by an expansion of the activated installed base to more than 175 global centers and ongoing integration of the recently-acquired IRRAflow product portfolio.

claims.claim: The company delivered 43% year-on-year growth in revenue to USD 12.1 million.
claims.comment: The source reports first quarter 2026 revenue of $12.1 million, representing 43% growth versus the first quarter of 2025.

claims.claim: This growth was driven by an expansion of the activated installed base to more than 175 global centers.
claims.comment: The source confirms the activated installed base is now over 175 global centers, but does not state that this expansion was the driver of the 43% revenue growth.

claims.claim: This growth was driven by ongoing integration of the recently-acquired IRRAflow product portfolio.
claims.comment: The source notes measurable revenue and cost synergies from IRRAflow integration and that IRRAS was acquired in November 2025, but does not explicitly attribute the 43% overall revenue growth to this integration as the driver.

cards.statement: Organic growth amounted to -50% year on year (25% for devices), while the gross margin expanded to 64% over the period on account of lower allowances for excess and obsolete inventory.

claims.claim: Organic growth amounted to -50% year on year.
claims.comment: The source states total organic growth was 16% year-over-year, not negative 50%.

claims.claim: Organic growth for devices was 25% year on year.
claims.comment: The headline and CEO commentary state 25% organic growth in devices; the year-on-year context is clear from the comparison to first quarter 2025.

claims.claim: The gross margin expanded to 64% over the period on account of lower allowances for excess and obsolete inventory.
claims.comment: The source reports gross margin of 64% for Q1 2026 versus 60% in Q1 2025 and attributes the increase primarily to lower excess and obsolete inventory.

cards.statement: Topline growth was driven by the neurosurgery navigation, therapy and access division, which contributed the vast majority of the company’s overall revenue and achieved 80% year-on-year growth, benefitting from contributions from the IRRAflow product line and the 3.0 operating room navigation software.

claims.claim: Topline growth was driven by the neurosurgery navigation, therapy and access division.
claims.comment: The source details that neurosurgery navigation, therapy and access revenue grew 80%, but does not state that this segment drove overall topline growth; that causal framing is not in the document.

claims.claim: The neurosurgery navigation, therapy and access division contributed the vast majority of the company’s overall revenue.
claims.comment: The source gives segment revenues: biologics and drug delivery $4.8m, neurosurgery navigation $5.9m, capital equipment and software $1.4m, totaling $12.1m. Neurosurgery navigation is the single largest segment but does not constitute a clear 'vast majority' of total revenue.

claims.claim: The neurosurgery navigation, therapy and access division achieved 80% year-on-year growth.
claims.comment: The source states neurosurgery navigation, therapy and access revenue increased 80% year-over-year.

claims.claim: This segment benefited from contributions from the IRRAflow product line and the 3.0 operating room navigation software.
claims.comment: The source attributes the increase in neurosurgery navigation, therapy and access revenue to additional revenues from IRRAflow product sales and the introduction of the 3.0 operating room navigation software.

cards.statement: Capital equipment and software revenue increased by 177% from a low base due to an increase in placements of ClearPoint navigation capital and software, IRRAflow control units, and Prism laser units.

claims.claim: Capital equipment and software revenue increased by 177% from a low base.
claims.comment: The source confirms a 177% increase in capital equipment and software revenue, but does not characterize the prior-year level as 'a low base'; that qualitative description is not sourced.

claims.claim: The increase in capital equipment and software revenue was due to an increase in placements of ClearPoint navigation capital and software, IRRAflow control units, and Prism laser units.
claims.comment: The source explicitly attributes the 177% increase to increased placements of ClearPoint navigation capital and software, IRRAflow control units, and Prism laser units.

cards.statement: Meanwhile, biologics and drug delivery revenue was broadly flat compared with the prior year.

claims.claim: Biologics and drug delivery revenue was broadly flat compared with the prior year.
claims.comment: The source shows biologics and drug delivery revenue increasing from $4.7m to $4.8m and describes this as a slight increase; characterizing this as 'broadly flat' is a reasonable paraphrase.

cards.statement: Meanwhile, the company continues to progress its clinical trial program, which now covers more than 60 active biopharma partners.

claims.claim: The company continues to progress its clinical trial program, which now covers more than 60 active biopharma partners.
claims.comment: The source notes continued clinical trial and regulatory progress across more than 60 active biopharma partners and refers to a portfolio of more than 60 partners and programs, supporting both ongoing progress and the partner count.

cards.statement: Notably, a submission for FDA approval has been made for the company’s Velocity Alpha MR High Speed Surgical Drill System.

claims.claim: A submission for FDA approval has been made for the company’s Velocity Alpha MR High Speed Surgical Drill System.
claims.comment: The source states that FDA clearance has already been obtained and the first clinical procedure completed for the Velocity Alpha MR High Speed Surgical Drill System; it does not mention a submission being made, which would be a different regulatory stage.

cards.statement: Elsewhere, the FDA issued a medical device license for the ClearPoint Neuro Navigation System, which covers both MRI-guidance and iCT guidance workflows, while the first commercial drug delivery case utilizing ClearPoint technology has been commenced in the Asia-Pacific region.

claims.claim: The FDA issued a medical device license for the ClearPoint Neuro Navigation System, which covers both MRI-guidance and iCT guidance workflows.
claims.comment: The source states that a Medical Device License was received from Health Canada for the ClearPoint Neuro Navigation System; it does not attribute this license to the FDA. The coverage of MRI-guidance and iCT workflows is correct, but the regulator is misidentified.

claims.claim: The first commercial drug delivery case utilizing ClearPoint technology has been commenced in the Asia-Pacific region.
claims.comment: The source notes completion of the first commercial drug delivery case using ClearPoint technology in the Asia-Pacific region; describing this as having been commenced is consistent with that event having taken place.

cards.statement: The company provided updated revenue guidance of USD 56 million for 2027.

claims.claim: The company provided updated revenue guidance of USD 56 million for 2027.
claims.comment: The source provides revenue guidance for 2026 of $52–56 million and discusses expectations that IRRAS integration could be cash neutral in 2027, but does not give revenue guidance for 2027 or a single-point figure of $56 million.

cards.statement: 3i Group delivered a total return of GBP 3.3 billion for the six months to 30 June 2025, representing a 13% return on opening shareholders funds.

claims.claim: 3i Group delivered a total return of GBP 3.3 billion for the six months to 30 June 2025, representing a 13% return on opening shareholders funds.
claims.comment: The source reports a total return of £3,291m (≈£3.3bn) and 13% on opening shareholders’ funds, but for the six months to 30 September 2025, not to 30 June 2025. The period end date is incorrect.

cards.statement: The private equity business generated gross investment returns of 14% for the period and accounted for the vast majority of the overall total return.

claims.claim: The private equity business generated gross investment returns of 14% for the period and accounted for the vast majority of the overall total return.
claims.comment: The source confirms the Private Equity business delivered a gross investment return of 14% for the period. However, it does not state that Private Equity accounted for the vast majority of the overall total return, so that portion is unsupported.

cards.statement: This was driven largely by Action, which continues to trade strongly.

claims.claim: This was driven largely by Action, which continues to trade strongly.
claims.comment: The source states that the Private Equity gross investment return was driven by Action, which continued to trade strongly. This supports both that Action was a major driver and that it continues to trade strongly.

cards.statement: The company’s new store expansion program is set for another record year with new stores in Switzerland and Romania being well received.

claims.claim: The company’s new store expansion program is set for another record year with new stores in Switzerland and Romania being well received.
claims.comment: The source notes that Action’s new store expansion programme is on track for another record year and that new stores in Switzerland and Romania have been very well received. This matches the claim.

cards.statement: Year to date like-for-like trading remains healthy despite weakening consumer confidence since the summer.

claims.claim: Year to date like-for-like trading remains healthy despite weakening consumer confidence since the summer.
claims.comment: The source says year-to-date like-for-like trading remains good despite weakening consumer confidence since the summer. Describing this as "healthy" is a reasonable paraphrase of "good".

cards.statement: Net sales for the nine months to 28 September 2025 amounted to EUR 11.2 billion, with like-for-like sales growth of 6.3%.

claims.claim: Net sales for the nine months to 28 September 2025 amounted to EUR 11.2 billion, with like-for-like sales growth of 6.3%.
claims.comment: The source reports net sales of €11,229m and LFL sales growth of 6.3% for the nine reporting periods ending on 28 September 2025. Rounding €11,229m to €11.2bn is acceptable.

cards.statement: Meanwhile, Action successfully completed several balance sheet transactions in October 2025.

claims.claim: Meanwhile, Action successfully completed several balance sheet transactions in October 2025.
claims.comment: The source describes two financing transactions completed by Action in October 2025. Referring to these as several balance sheet transactions is a fair characterisation.

cards.statement: The company repriced EUR 3.1 billion of existing term debt, extending maturities and generating meaningful annual interest cost savings, while also raising an incremental EUR 1.6 billion of new term loan.

claims.claim: The company repriced EUR 3.1 billion of existing term debt, extending maturities and generating meaningful annual interest cost savings, while also raising an incremental EUR 1.6 billion of new term loan.
claims.comment: The source confirms Action raised €1.6bn of incremental term loan debt and repriced €3.1bn of existing term loan debt, extending the maturity of a portion and generating annual interest cost savings of €14m. Describing the savings as meaningful is interpretive but consistent.

cards.statement: Action also completed a pro-rata redemption of shares, which generated significant proceeds for 3i.

claims.claim: Action also completed a pro-rata redemption of shares, which generated significant proceeds for 3i.
claims.comment: The source states Action completed a capital restructuring with a pro-rata redemption of shares, returning £944m of gross proceeds to 3i. Calling these proceeds significant is a reasonable qualitative description.

cards.statement: A portion of these proceeds was redeployed to acquire a further 2.2% stake in the business, which together with an earlier 2.2% stake purchase from GIC, raised 3i’s stake in Action to 62.3%.

claims.claim: A portion of these proceeds was redeployed to acquire a further 2.2% stake in the business, which together with an earlier 2.2% stake purchase from GIC, raised 3i’s stake in Action to 62.3%.
claims.comment: The source confirms 3i acquired 2.2% of Action equity from GIC in September 2025 and used £755m of the October 2025 proceeds to acquire a further 2.2%, increasing its ownership to 62.3%. This matches the claim.

cards.statement: Elsewhere, within the private equity portfolio, 3i completed the sale of MPM and signed an exit of MAIT during the period, which generated gross money multiples of 3.2x and 2.8x, respectively.

claims.claim: Elsewhere, within the private equity portfolio, 3i completed the sale of MPM and signed an exit of MAIT during the period, which generated gross money multiples of 3.2x and 2.8x, respectively.
claims.comment: The source states that 3i completed the realisation of MPM and signed the realisation of MAIT, with sterling money multiples of 3.2x and 2.8x respectively. This supports the claim.

cards.statement: On the infrastructure side, gross investment returns stood at 9% for the period, outperforming expectations for the six-month period.

claims.claim: On the infrastructure side, gross investment returns stood at 9% for the period, outperforming expectations for the six-month period.
claims.comment: The source confirms a gross investment return of 9% for the Infrastructure business. It also notes that the infrastructure asset portfolio within 3iN outperformed its expected returns, but does not explicitly say that the 9% gross investment return itself outperformed expectations. The outperformance wording is therefore only partially supported.

cards.statement: Performance was driven primarily by share price gains at 3i Infrastructure plc, which continues to report positive performance across its portfolio, including meaningful gains on its investment in TCR.

claims.claim: Performance was driven primarily by share price gains at 3i Infrastructure plc, which continues to report positive performance across its portfolio, including meaningful gains on its investment in TCR.
claims.comment: The source confirms performance was driven primarily by a 14% increase in 3i Infrastructure plc’s share price and notes a significant valuation uplift in TCR. However, it does not state that 3i Infrastructure plc "continues to report positive performance across its portfolio"; that broader characterisation is not in the text.

cards.statement: In light of the overall good performance of the portfolio, 3i declared a dividend of GBP 0.365 per share, which will be paid in January 2026.

claims.claim: In light of the overall good performance of the portfolio, 3i declared a dividend of GBP 0.365 per share, which will be paid in January 2026.
claims.comment: The source confirms a dividend of 36.5 pence per share to be paid in January 2026. It does not state that this was declared "in light of the overall good performance of the portfolio"; that causal framing is not supported.

cards.statement: Looking ahead, management maintains its cautious stance on capital deployment into new investments, but remains open to selective allocations to lower-risk reinvestments in existing portfolio companies.

claims.claim: Looking ahead, management maintains its cautious stance on capital deployment into new investments, but remains open to selective allocations to lower-risk reinvestments in existing portfolio companies.
claims.comment: The source states that 3i remains cautious in deploying capital into new investment but will continue to allocate selectively, including to lower-risk reinvestments in businesses it knows and trusts. This supports the claim.

cards.statement: HICL Infrastructure’s performance for the five months to 28 February 2026 was positive and largely in line with expectations.

claims.claim: HICL Infrastructure’s performance for the five months to 28 February 2026 was positive and largely in line with expectations.
claims.comment: The period covered is 1 October 2025 to 28 February 2026 (five months). The source describes portfolio and operational performance as in line with expectations and robust, which supports characterising performance as positive and largely in line with expectations.

cards.statement: Across the portfolio, operational performance was robust, with EBITDA growth driven by capital expenditure, and resilient cashflow generation supporting HCIL’s dividend program.

claims.claim: Across the portfolio, operational performance was robust, with EBITDA growth driven by capital expenditure, and resilient cashflow generation supporting HCIL’s dividend program.
claims.comment: The source supports robust operational performance, capex programmes driving EBITDA growth, and cash generation underpinning dividend cover and the dividend outlook. However, the draft contains a typo in the company name (HCIL instead of HICL), and the specific phrase 'supporting HCIL’s dividend program' is a paraphrase of dividend cover and outlook rather than a direct statement; overall sense is supported but the name is inaccurate.

cards.statement: Across the portfolio, growth investments continue to perform well, with significant investment in expansion programs driving EBITDA growth that continues to perform in line with budgets.

claims.claim: Across the portfolio, growth investments continue to perform well, with significant investment in expansion programs driving EBITDA growth that continues to perform in line with budgets.
claims.comment: The source states that HICL’s growth investments continue to perform well, progressing significant expansion capex programmes and delivering EBITDA in line with expectations. This supports most of the claim. However, the wording 'across the portfolio' overgeneralises, as the source refers specifically to growth investments rather than the entire portfolio, and it mentions expectations rather than budgets.

cards.statement: Among the significant holdings, London St. Pancras High Speed performed well during the period, with international train path bookings slightly ahead of forecast.

claims.claim: Among the significant holdings, London St. Pancras High Speed performed well during the period, with international train path bookings slightly ahead of forecast.
claims.comment: The source explicitly notes that London St. Pancras High Speed performed well and that international train path bookings were slightly ahead of forecast, matching the claim.

cards.statement: On the commercial front, progress has been made on adding a second international operator on the route, while Virgin Trains recently announced its intentions for cross-Channel operations from St. Pancras.

claims.claim: On the commercial front, progress has been made on adding a second international operator on the route, while Virgin Trains recently announced its intentions for cross-Channel operations from St. Pancras.
claims.comment: The source describes progress toward a potential second international operator, including announcements by Virgin Trains regarding its intentions for cross-Channel operations from St. Pancras, which supports this claim.

cards.statement: Elsewhere, Fortysouth delivered 16 new towers during the period and is actively progressing additional co-location opportunities, both of which are expected to support continued growth in EBITDA and valuation gains.

claims.claim: Elsewhere, Fortysouth delivered 16 new towers during the period and is actively progressing additional co-location opportunities, both of which are expected to support continued growth in EBITDA and valuation gains.
claims.comment: The source confirms Fortysouth delivered 16 new towers, is progressing incremental co-location opportunities, and that these are expected to support continued EBITDA growth in line with valuation assumptions. However, the draft adds 'valuation gains', which is not stated in the source and goes beyond the evidence.

cards.statement: The company also recently completed an oversubscribed refinancing, which will lead to a reduction in debt servicing costs.

claims.claim: The company also recently completed an oversubscribed refinancing, which will lead to a reduction in debt servicing costs.
claims.comment: The source confirms an accretive refinancing that was about 30% oversubscribed and enabled a step-down in debt margins earlier than forecast, implying lower interest costs. The claim that this will lead to a reduction in debt servicing costs is a reasonable inference. However, the source does not explicitly state 'debt servicing costs', so that part is interpretive rather than directly supported.

cards.statement: Meanwhile, Affinity Water appointed a new CEO with significant sector experience and stands to benefit from the UK government’s recently published white paper on water sector reform.

claims.claim: Meanwhile, Affinity Water appointed a new CEO with significant sector experience and stands to benefit from the UK government’s recently published white paper on water sector reform.
claims.comment: The source confirms the appointment of a new CEO with significant sector experience and notes that many aspects of the white paper are expected to be beneficial for strong performers such as Affinity Water. However, the phrase 'stands to benefit' generalises this expectation and could be read as stronger or broader than the source, which is more conditional and framed around strong performers in general.

cards.statement: In November 2025, GP Industries announced that it intends to shift production capacity to its manufacturing sites in Southeast Asia to serve the US market amid tariffs and rising geopolitical tensions.

claims.claim: In November 2025, GP Industries announced that it intends to shift production capacity to its manufacturing sites in Southeast Asia to serve the US market amid tariffs and rising geopolitical tensions.
claims.comment: The press release is dated 13 November 2025 and states that GP Industries is shifting production capacity to Southeast Asia to navigate US tariffs and geopolitical tensions, and that Southeast Asia capacity will be ramped up to serve the US market. The draft’s wording about an announcement in November 2025 and the intent to shift capacity to serve the US market amid tariffs and tensions is a faithful paraphrase.

cards.statement: The company currently operates three facilities in Malaysia, two in Vietnam, and one in Thailand, alongside two other plants in the UK and one plant in China, which will now focus primarily on the European and Asian markets.

claims.claim: The company currently operates three facilities in Malaysia, two in Vietnam, and one in Thailand, alongside two other plants in the UK and one plant in China, which will now focus primarily on the European and Asian markets.
claims.comment: The source confirms three facilities in Malaysia, two in Vietnam, one in Thailand, and two plants in the UK, and that the China facility will focus primarily on European and Asian markets. It does not state that there is only one plant in China; it refers to a singular China facility but gives no count. The phrase "one plant in China" adds a specific number not supported by the source, while the rest of the claim is supported.

cards.statement: The capacity adjustments are intended to streamline supply chains to meet country-of-origin requirements while maintaining cost competitiveness.

claims.claim: The capacity adjustments are intended to streamline supply chains to meet country-of-origin requirements while maintaining cost competitiveness.
claims.comment: The source explains that Southeast Asia capacity will be ramped up for the US and China will focus on Europe and Asia, and explicitly states that the move will streamline supply chains to meet country-of-origin requirements and maintain cost competitiveness. This matches the claim.

cards.statement: Meanwhile, Gold Peak Technology (parent of GP Industries) is planning an investment program in Johor, Malaysia, to produce next-generation batteries to support data centres.

claims.claim: Meanwhile, Gold Peak Technology (parent of GP Industries) is planning an investment program in Johor, Malaysia, to produce next-generation batteries to support data centres.
claims.comment: The source confirms that GP Industries is owned 86.18% by Hong Kong-listed Gold Peak Technology Group and that Gold Peak is planning a multi-million-dollar investment in Johor to produce next-generation battery to support data centres. The draft correctly captures the parent relationship, the Johor location, and the purpose. However, it introduces the phrase "investment program," which implies an ongoing or structured programme not specified in the source; the source only mentions a planned investment. Hence, most of the claim is supported but that nuance is not.

cards.statement: GP Industries is the second-largest producer of consumer batteries globally, producing over 6 billion batteries annually, which are sold through 1 million outlets worldwide.

claims.claim: GP Industries is the second-largest producer of consumer batteries globally, producing over 6 billion batteries annually, which are sold through 1 million outlets worldwide.
claims.comment: The source describes GP Industries as the world’s second-largest producer of consumer batteries and states that it produces over six billion batteries annually sold through one million outlets worldwide. This directly supports the claim.

cards.statement: In May 2026, ClearPoint Neuro reported its financial results for the first quarter of 2026.

claims.claim: In May 2026, ClearPoint Neuro reported its financial results for the first quarter of 2026.
claims.comment: The press release is dated May 13, 2026 and announces financial results for the first quarter ended March 31, 2026.

cards.statement: The company delivered 43% year-on-year growth in revenue to USD 12.1 million, driven by an expansion of the activated installed base to more than 175 global centers and ongoing integration of the recently-acquired IRRAflow product portfolio.

claims.claim: The company delivered 43% year-on-year growth in revenue to USD 12.1 million.
claims.comment: The source reports total revenue of $12.1 million for Q1 2026 versus $8.5 million in Q1 2025, an increase of $3.6 million or 43%.

claims.claim: The 43% year-on-year growth in revenue was driven by an expansion of the activated installed base to more than 175 global centers and ongoing integration of the recently-acquired IRRAflow product portfolio.
claims.comment: The source confirms the activated installed base includes over 175 global centers and mentions measurable revenue and cost synergies from IRRAflow integration, but it does not state that these factors specifically *drove* the 43% overall revenue growth. Drivers cited for specific segments include IRRAflow product sales and 3.0 OR software, not installed base expansion per se.

cards.statement: Organic growth amounted to 16% year on year (25% for devices), while the gross margin expanded to 64% over the period on account of lower allowances for excess and obsolete inventory.

claims.claim: Organic growth amounted to 16% year on year.
claims.comment: The highlights state that reported Q1 revenue of $12.1m represented 16% year-over-year total organic growth compared with Q1 2025.

claims.claim: Organic growth amounted to 25% year on year for devices.
claims.comment: The headline and CEO commentary state record revenue including 25% organic growth in devices; this is clearly device organic growth for the period.

claims.claim: The gross margin expanded to 64% over the period on account of lower allowances for excess and obsolete inventory.
claims.comment: The source reports gross margin of 64% for Q1 2026 versus 60% in Q1 2025 and attributes the increase primarily to lower excess and obsolete inventory.

cards.statement: Topline growth was driven by the neurosurgery navigation, therapy and access division, which achieved an 80% increase in revenue to USD 5.9 million, benefitting from contributions from the IRRAflow product line and the 3.0 operating room navigation software.

claims.claim: Topline growth was driven by the neurosurgery navigation, therapy and access division, which achieved an 80% increase in revenue to USD 5.9 million.
claims.comment: The source confirms neurosurgery navigation, therapy and access revenue increased 80% to $5.9m. However, it does not state that overall topline growth was *driven* by this division, even though the growth is large; that causal framing is not explicitly supported.

claims.claim: The neurosurgery navigation, therapy and access division benefitted from contributions from the IRRAflow product line and the 3.0 operating room navigation software.
claims.comment: The source states the 80% increase was driven by additional revenues from IRRAflow product sales and the introduction of the 3.0 operating room navigation software, which implies the division benefited from these contributions.

cards.statement: Capital equipment and software revenue increased by 177% from a low base due to an increase in placements of ClearPoint navigation capital and software, IRRAflow control units, and Prism laser units.

claims.claim: Capital equipment and software revenue increased by 177% from a low base due to an increase in placements of ClearPoint navigation capital and software, IRRAflow control units, and Prism laser units.
claims.comment: The source confirms capital equipment and software revenue increased 177% to $1.4m from $0.5m and attributes this to increased placements of ClearPoint navigation capital and software, IRRAflow control units, and Prism laser units. The phrase "from a low base" is not stated in the source, though it is consistent with the small prior-year figure; this portion is interpretive rather than sourced.

cards.statement: Meanwhile, biologics and drug delivery revenue was broadly flat compared with the prior year.

claims.claim: Biologics and drug delivery revenue was broadly flat compared with the prior year.
claims.comment: The source shows biologics and drug delivery revenue increased slightly from $4.7m to $4.8m, which reasonably supports describing it as broadly flat.

cards.statement: Meanwhile, the company continues to progress its clinical trial program, which now covers more than 60 active biopharma partners.

claims.claim: The company continues to progress its clinical trial program, which now covers more than 60 active biopharma partners.
claims.comment: The highlights note continued clinical trial and regulatory progress across more than 60 active biopharma partners, and the CEO reiterates a portfolio of more than 60 partners and programs.

cards.statement: Notably, FDA clearance was received and first clinical procedures completed utilizing the company's Velocity Alpha MR High Speed Surgical Drill System.

claims.claim: FDA clearance was received and first clinical procedures completed utilizing the company's Velocity Alpha MR High Speed Surgical Drill System.
claims.comment: The source states FDA clearance and successful completion of the first clinical procedure utilizing the Velocity Alpha MR High Speed Surgical Drill System, and the CEO notes the drill has now been used clinically for the first time.

cards.statement: Elsewhere, Health Canada issued a medical device license for the ClearPoint Neuro Navigation System, which covers both MRI-guidance and iCT guidance workflows, while the first commercial drug delivery case utilizing ClearPoint technology was completed in the Asia-Pacific region.

claims.claim: Health Canada issued a medical device license for the ClearPoint Neuro Navigation System, which covers both MRI-guidance and iCT guidance workflows.
claims.comment: The source reports receipt of a Medical Device License from Health Canada for the ClearPoint Neuro Navigation System, covering both MRI-guidance and iCT guidance workflows.

claims.claim: The first commercial drug delivery case utilizing ClearPoint technology was completed in the Asia-Pacific region.
claims.comment: The highlights state completion of the first commercial drug delivery case utilizing ClearPoint technology in the Asia-Pacific region.

cards.statement: The company provided updated revenue guidance of USD 52-56 million for 2026.

claims.claim: The company provided updated revenue guidance of USD 52-56 million for 2026.
claims.comment: The source states the company estimates 2026 revenue between $52.0m and $56.0m. It does not specify that this guidance is an *update* versus prior guidance; the word "updated" is not supported.
